NEWS FROM THE BOARD March 2025 NEWS FROM THE BOARD A monthly newsletter from the Ada County Board of Commissioners Welcome to the monthly newsletter from the Ada County Board of Commissioners. We are happy to share information on significant news and events in Ada County. Ryan Davidson - Commissioner Rod Beck - Chairman Tom Dayley - Commissioner PROFESSIONAL SOCCER COMING TO IDAHO Games will begin in March of 2026 The professional sports landscape in Idaho is changing dramatically. Ada County Commissioners officially broke ground on March 27, 2025 on a new soccer facility that will be home to Idaho’s first professional soccer team. The groundbreaking took place in front of the Turf Club on Ada County’s Expo Idaho property. The former horse racing track, which has been mostly idle for ten years, is being transformed into world class soccer fields. Professional soccer games will begin in March of 2026! “Professional soccer is good business for the soccer folks, but more importantly for Ada County it allows us to best utilize our properties in ways that will benefit the lives of countless people now and into the future.” Rod Beck, Ada County Commission Chairman. “This project is a labor of love for Boise and the entire Treasure Valley,” said Brad Stith Boise Pro Soccer CEO & Co-Founder. “This is built for our community, and most importantly it’s built by our community.”

# Page 2^page=2
“The USL will be a league that will match the ambitions of our fans,” said Justin Papadakis with the United Soccer League. “That means our fans deserve a first-class fan experience. Every game needs to be a match of consequence. Our players will live here and raise their families here.” “The downstream effects of having a men’s and soon to be a professional women’s team here in our community is difficult to encapsulate,” said Bill Taylor, Vice Chair, U.S. Youth Soccer & Boise Pro Soccer Co-Founder. “The direct impact to our children who will now be able to watch live professional games, attend training sessions, participate in camps, and be scouted and identified, will provide opportunities they have never had.” The name of the team and the players have yet to be determined at this very early stage of the game – but it’s in the works. This is all happening thanks to a 30-year lease agreement between Ada County and Boise Pro Soccer. The agreement signed February 21, 2025, means Boise Pro Soccer will pay the county $150,000 annually for the lease with a portion of the income generated by Boise Pro Soccer being used to maintain the adjacent Park at Expo Idaho. No tax dollars are being used on this project. Boise Pro Soccer will remodel and retrofit both the Grandstands and the Turf Club. Ada County will retain ownership of the property. 2

4 NEW DRIVER’S LICENSE OFFICE OPENS IN STAR The new Star driver’s license office is officially open at Star City Hall. Ada County Sheriff Matt Clifford, Star Mayor Trevor Chadwick, and Ada County Assessor Rebecca Arnold cut the ribbon to commemorate the opening of the new facility on March 18, 2025. This new location brings essential licensing services closer to our growing Ada County communities. “We are so pleased to be offering this service to residents in northern Ada County, in the same office as our Star DMV,” said Ada County Assessor Rebecca Arnold. “It’s important that this service, along with our DMV services for vehicle titles and registration, be easily accessible to all of our county residents.” Ada County operates five Motor Vehicle DMV offices and now with Star’s Driver’s License Office - three locations where you can get or renew your driver’s license. In Idaho, DMV and Driver’s License offices are two separate functions. DMV offices are run by County Assessor’s Offices; Driver’s License Offices are run by the County Sheriff Offices. Learn more about Ada County’s DMV services, including locations where our staff can help you in person, and information on vehicle registration and titles here: adacounty.id.gov/assessor/dmv-registrations-titles/ Left to Right: Jasna Huntington, Law Enforcement Records Technician III; Susan Romero, Driver’s License Supervisor; Ada County Sheriff Matt Clifford; Ada County Assessor Rebecca Arnold; Star, Idaho Mayor Trevor Chadwick; Andrew Marini, Driver’s License Manager; Kari LaCroix, Driver’s License Supervisor; Clayton Hall, Ada County Assessor, DMV Division Manager. Tiffany Mercurio, Driver’s Licensing Law Enforcement Records Technician II and Jasna Huntington, Law Enforcement Records Technician III FOLLOWING THREE OPEN HOUSES FOR PUBLIC INPUT ADA COUNTY’S ZONING ORDINANCE CHANGES HEADING TO PLANNING AND ZONING THEN THE BOARD OF ADA COUNTY COMMISSIONERS In February and March, Ada County Development Services held three open houses to discuss the new Zoning Ordinance with the public. More than 200 people attended these open houses. Staff listened to their concerns and made a number of changes to the ordinance based on the feedback we received. Now, the ordinance will go to a public hearing. First, it will go before the Planning and Zoning Commission on April 24th. That will be followed by the Board of County Commissioners on June 11, 2025. Thank you to everyone who provided valuable input.

ADA COUNTY RECOGNIZES PROCUREMENT MONTH Vendor Fair Draws Diverse Businesses and Suppliers Ada County Procurement held its 19th Annual Vendor Fair on March 20, 2025. The event allows vendors who work with Ada County to showcase their best and newest products, services, and items that can be purchased on cooperative contracts. The popular annual event is an opportunity for those charged with making important purchasing decisions to examine products and discuss pricing trends with vendors prior to making decisions that will impact next year’s county budget. Thank you to our vendors, and to Procurement staff for coordinating this event each year. PROCUREMENT MONTH The Idaho Public Purchasing Association and other public professional procurement associations throughout the world engage in special efforts during March, to inform the public about the importance of the role played by professionals in business, industry and government. March is Procurement Month. Thank you to our dedicated staff: Pictured Left-Right: Ryan Blaine; Evan Amidan; Kathleen Corless; Robyn Swaney; Alyssa Ellington; Ada County Commission Chairman Rod Beck; Ada County Commissioner Tom Dayley; Ken Sinclair; Ada County Commissioner Ryan Davidson; Ada County Procurement Director Bob Perkins 5

WEEDING OUT YOUR LAWN’S COMPETITION Getting rid of weeds is our kind of lawnlawn enforcement Spring has arrived, bringing with it the emergence of early-season noxious weeds in Ada County. At this stage, many of these invasive plants are in their rosette form—making them particularly vulnerable and easier to control. This is the ideal time to remove them before they spread. One such weed is poison hemlock, a highly toxic plant that can be deadly if ingested. It is identified by its tall stalks with small white flowers and distinctive, purple- spotted stems. In early spring, it emerges as dense stands of dark green rosettes with fern-like leaves. To effectively remove Poison hemlock, dig or pull the plant, ensuring you extract at least eight inches of its root to prevent regrowth. Wear heavy-duty, chemical- resistant rubber gloves, and thoroughly clean any tools after use. This is also an effective time to treat rosettes with herbicide for long-term control. Sam Brockway Program and Education Specialist DO NOT BURN Poison hemlock, as inhaling the smoke can be hazardous. 6

CERTIFIED GOVERNMENT FINANCIAL MANAGER MONTH Idaho counties are required to carry out specific tasks set forth by the legislature. In Ada County, this has always been done with a laser focus on frugality and value. On March 18, 2025, the Board of Commissioners recognized some outstanding staff who are stewards of the county’s financial efficiency and transparency. The Board of Commissioners designated March as Certified Government Financial Manager Month. Thank you to these public servants who help us to be accountable to all taxpayers every day of every year. Pictured Left-Right: Tim Sturgess, Ada County Controller; Katie Carnduff, Ada County Operations Finance Manager; Ada County Commissioner Ryan Davidson; Sarah Lund, Accounting Manager; Ada County Commission Chairman Rod Beck; Ada County Commissioner Tom Dayley EMS MILESTONE During his 20 years with Ada County Paramedics, the word most frequently associated with Robert Vander Stelt is insightful. As a well-respected Field Captain, Robert takes a quiet approach to much of his work. You’d be mistaken if you read that silence as a lack of skill or ability. Quite the contrary is true. Robert’s contributions frequently come at the end of long, contentious discussions after he’s heard what the room has to say. Then, Robert is ready to share thoughts with a different perspective that are additive to the conversation. Many of the answers produced by our leadership group are significantly improved by having Robert’s insight and perspective. This is the sort of approach Robert uses in all his professional dealings. It is effective and highly valued. Thank you for 20 years of making sure Ada County Paramedics is kept in the care of your thoughts, perspective, and abilities. - Deputy Chief of Operations John Blake Pictured Left-Right: Ada County Paramedics Chief Shawn Rayne; Ada County Paramedics Field Captain Robert Vander Stelt; Ada County Commissioner Ryan Davidson; Ada County Commissioner Tom Dayley; Ada County Paramedics Deputy Chief John Blake 7

Thank you to the Kiwanis Club of Meridian for inviting Ada County Commission Chairman Rod Beck to speak at the March luncheon. Chairman Beck shared information with club members on upcoming projects happening in Ada County including The Park at Expo Idaho, Professional Soccer, and the essential services provided to each of our six sister cities. WATCH OUR PROGRESS ON THE PARK AT EXPO IDAHO Monthly videos highlight the amazing transformation You’ve read a lot about professional soccer coming to Idaho in this edition of the Ada County newsletter but that’s not all that’s happening on the 240-acre Expo Idaho property. The Park at Expo Idaho will also be completed in 2026. Each month we provide you with a progress video showing the transformation of approximately fifty acres on the same grounds. Watch our videos on Ada County’s YouTube: THE PARK AT EXPO IDAHO CONSTRUCTION You can also check us out on Facebook and the website WATCH THE PROGRESS ADA COUNTY GOVERNMENT In addition to elected offices, Ada County government includes twelve individual departments. Each department provides important services to our residents in Star, Eagle, Meridian, Boise, Garden City, Kuna, and Unincorporated Ada County. These services include law enforcement protection, emergency preparedness, election services, parks & waterways, indigent services, juvenile services, solid waste management, the Western Idaho Fair, Weed, Pest & Mosquito Abatement and more. Learn more about the services provided to you by Ada County - www.adacounty.id.gov/ 8
